sections.h2: Where to go for property tax
sections.html:
Neither of the two county offices decides the rate; the County Commission does that every year. The Property Assessor puts a value on each parcel and sits at 3411 Highway 126, Suite 103, Blountville (423-323-6455, open weekdays, eight to five). Money goes to the Trustee at 1651 Blountville Boulevard, Suite 104, Blountville, TN 37617 (423-323-6464, same schedule).

Two seasonal Trustee counters help in the cities. In Bristol, find Room 139 at 801 Anderson Street, staffed Thursday and Friday. In Kingsport, go to #101 at 225 West Center Street, Monday through Wednesday. Each is open only between October 1 and March 15, breaks for lunch from 1:30 to 2:30 p.m., and closes on holidays and election days.

Houses within Bristol, Kingsport or Bluff City can carry a second, city bill. The Trustee's FAQ covers this. The city sets its own rate and due date, so ask city hall.

Up in Tennessee's northeast corner on the Virginia line, Sullivan County is home to Kingsport, its largest city, plus Bristol, Bluff City and part of Johnson City. Blountville serves as county seat. Because three school systems operate here (Bristol Tennessee City Schools, Kingsport City School District and Sullivan County Schools), the zone a buyer gets depends on the address.

As of July 2025 the population was 163,759, a 3.5% rise since April 2020, and there were 77,633 housing units with 72.1% lived in by their owners. Owner-occupied homes carry a typical value of $213,300, rents run around $889 a month, and 771 building permits were issued in 2025.

sections.h2: How the tax bill is figured
sections.html:
The Trustee's FAQ gives the formula: assessed value is 25 percent of the property's value, and the county rate is applied to that figure. For 2025 the posted county rate is $1.6129 per $100 of assessed value, and a city can add its own levy.

A bill covers a single calendar year. Business furniture and equipment are taxable as well, and business owners file a personal property schedule annually. Property values will be reset in the next county-wide reappraisal, scheduled for 2027.

sections.h2: Due dates and ways to pay
sections.html:
The due date is the first Monday in October, and nothing is added until the end of February. Paying early earns no discount. When March 1 arrives, any unpaid balance is delinquent and 1.5 percent interest is tacked on monthly.

Sullivan County tax calendar
DateWhat happens
Late SeptemberCourtesy notices mailed
October 1Bank of Tennessee payments begin
First Monday in OctoberTaxes due
February 26, 2027Last day to pay at the bank
February 28Last day without interest
March 1Delinquent, 1.5% monthly interest
March 15Last day at the Trustee before transfer to Clerk and Master

Ways to pay include:

  • In person in Blountville, Bristol or Kingsport
  • By mail to PO Box 550, Blountville, TN 37617, or the Blountville drop box
  • Online or by phone, with a card fee of 2.5 percent or an e-check fee of $1.25, both kept by the processor
  • At Bank of Tennessee branches with the notice, cash or check only

You may pay in installments between October 1 and February 28, but tracking what is left is up to you. A notice is not required by law, which means a bill that never shows up still collects interest, so phone the Trustee if yours is missing.

A practical routine for a seller: in late September watch for the courtesy notice, pay in October or November if you want the bill off your mind, and keep the receipt. If you plan to list in winter, paying before closing day means the payoff request at the table is a simple confirmation and not a scramble. Anyone paying at a bank should remember that the bank counter closes a couple of days before the Trustee's last day without interest, so the office or the mail is the safer choice near the deadline.

Phone the Assessor's office before anything else. A dispute that stays open goes to the county equalization board, set to meet June 1 on the state schedule. The state board is the next step, and its deadline is August 1 or 45 days after the local board mails its notice, whichever comes later. If your notice arrived late, call 615-401-7883 to confirm the window.

State guidance favors sales of comparable homes, with the gaps in size, age, condition and location accounted for. You can add an appraisal. Simply saying the house is overvalued without a number rarely persuades anyone. Meanwhile the undisputed part of the bill is still due on time, and so is any older delinquent tax.

A state rebate is available to owners who live in the home and are 65 or older, disabled, or a qualifying disabled former service member or that person's widowed spouse. For elderly and disabled applicants, combined household income, spouse included, cannot top $38,470. Take proof of income, your Social Security card, and proof of residency and age. To make an appointment, call 423-323-6470 or 423-323-6469.

Each year the signed voucher goes back to a Trustee office by April 5, not to a bank branch. A tax freeze program does not exist in Sullivan County.

Greenbelt and Forestry assessments are also run out of the Assessor's office. On the state calendar, greenbelt applications are due March 15 and exemption applications May 20. Owners of acreage should ask the Assessor about both before listing the property.

Business furnishings or equipment you own on January 1 can trigger personal property tax even if the shop later closes. Closing the business formally with the right agencies is what stops the bill.

The notice goes to whoever owned the house on January 1, even if it sells later that year. Buyers should still make sure the tax gets paid on time and follow the settlement statement for how it is divided. With an escrow account, the mortgage company receives the bill.

Owing tax means clearing the balance with the Trustee ahead of closing. Only a court order, or an assessment change by the State Board or the Assessor, can remove interest, so waivers are rare. Title companies typically pay the Trustee from your sale proceeds, which makes a payoff figure a few days early worth requesting. If March 1 is near, a cash sale can close faster than a financed one and stop interest from building. For an in-person payment, take the notice with you, since it carries your parcel details.

faqs.q: What is the Sullivan County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The Trustee's 2025 county levy is $1.6129 per $100 of assessed value. Assessment is 25 percent of value, and any city tax comes on top.

faqs.q: Is there a discount for paying Sullivan County taxes early?
faqs.a: None is offered. You can pay without penalty any time from October 1 through February 28, and installments are allowed in that stretch.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Sullivan County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Go to the Trustee in Blountville, or use the Bristol and Kingsport counters during their October 1 to March 15 season. Bank of Tennessee branches accept cash or checks if you bring the notice.

faqs.q: Does Sullivan County offer a property tax freeze?
faqs.a: Not at present. The state relief rebate is there for qualifying seniors, owners with disabilities and disabled former service members instead.

faqs.q: When is the next Sullivan County reappraisal?
faqs.a: 2027. Revaluation notices typically arrive in spring of a reappraisal year.
